[PATH:empirical] Empirical study comparing scaling trajectories of current transformer-based LLMs (e.g., GPT-4, Llama 3) against human-level benchmarks (e.g., ARC-AGI, MMLU, and novel reasoning tasks) over a 10-year period, with controlled compute budgets. — Directly tests whether continued scaling under current architectures approaches human-level general intelligence, or whether performance plateaus, indicating a need for architectural innovation.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical analysis of sample efficiency bounds in transformer architectures, building on the 'scaling laws' literature (Kaplan et al., 2020; Hoffmann et al., 2022) and extending to compute-optimal regimes with novel attention or memory mechanisms (e.g., Mamba, linear attention). — Provides formal limits on how much sample efficiency can be improved via architectural changes, and whether such improvements are necessary to bridge the gap to human-level intelligence within the 20-year horizon.

[PATH:literature] Literature review of historical scaling trends in AI (e.g., from CNNs to Transformers) and their relationship to general intelligence benchmarks, including surveys of meta-learning and few-shot learning architectures. — Contextualizes the hypothesis by examining past instances where scaling alone failed to achieve general capabilities, and where architectural innovations (e.g., attention, residual connections) were pivotal, informing the likelihood of similar necessity in the next 20 years.

[PATH:theoretical] Systematic literature review and meta-analysis of neuroscientific correlates of consciousness (e.g., integrated information theory, recurrent processing theory) applied to current AI capabilities — Compiling evidence on whether consciousness-like properties (e.g., phenomenal binding, metacognition) are uniquely associated with general problem-solving abilities in biological systems can clarify if they are causally required for AGI or merely correlated epiphenomena.

[PATH:empirical] Comparative analysis of AI performance on 'consciousness-requiring' tasks (e.g., subjective report, counterfactual reasoning, self-modeling) in systems with and without explicit consciousness models — Directly testing whether systems lacking any functional consciousness model can achieve human-level AGI on these tasks within 20 years would provide strong confirmatory or refutatory evidence for the hypothesis.
